A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 32 pages in each version, including equations, 15 figures, nine tables, and Appendix A, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original CompoSuite simulation results on compositional data generation, policy success, iterative improvement, representation analyses, and online RL, plus runtime measurements in Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 retains the original CompoSuite experiments, representation analyses, online RL comparisons, and appendix runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same factor-specific encoders and decoders, conditioned diffusion transformer, TD3-BC validation, and threshold-based iterative bootstrapping procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same expert CompoSuite data, IIWA-only and multi-robot manipulation tasks, and two rare-success tasks for online RL. Physical-robot and visual-observation evaluations remain future work.

E2.justification: Figure 5 retains Hardcoded Compositional RL, Semantic + Compositional RL, Monolithic/SynthER, Standard DiT, and Semantic DiT comparators. RLPD, SAC, and expert-data comparisons also retain their membership in the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same task splits, 14/64 and 56/256 training regimes, dataset sizes, model configurations, training budgets, metrics, policy-selection rules, and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The tokenization ablations, task-difficulty breakdowns, intervention and attention analyses, rare-success dataset analysis, and training-task scaling study are retained with the same evidence in Figures 5–13.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 retains three diffusion seeds with five RL seeds each and 15 seeds for static RL baselines. Standard-error reporting and the seed information throughout Appendix A are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched results in Figures 5–13 and Table 8 are unchanged. For example, Section 4.2 still reports 55% success for Semantic + Compositional DiT after four improvement iterations. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The MDP and task-graph definitions, diffusion and attention equations, and Appendix A.4 runtime derivation are retained. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added, removed, or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain their claims. v5 Section 7 preserves v4 Section 6's contributions concerning learned compositional structure, generation for unseen task combinations, and iterative self-improvement.

C2.justification: v4 already acknowledges absent physical-robot evaluation. v5 Section 6 adds that evaluating hundreds of task combinations would likely require multiple platforms, diverse configurations, and repeated evaluations across tasks and improvement iterations. Existing state-based and environment-interaction limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A's implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware, runtime information, and task lists are identical apart from running headers. The project website disclosure for code and visualizations is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the references retain the same cited works and methodological positioning relative to compositional policies, SynthER, and compositional world models. No novelty claims or cited-work membership change.

P1.justification: v5 separates existing limitations into Section 6, 'Limitations and Future Work,' and moves the retained conclusion to Section 7. It adds a short limitations expansion, publication/review text, and limited wording edits.

P2.justification: Publication headers and additional front matter accompany text reflow, including Figure 5 moving from page 8 to page 9. All figure graphics, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 already disclosed the absence of physical-robot testing and other applicability limits. v5 makes these limitations easier to find and explains the concrete evaluation burden of extending its large task space to physical platforms. This modestly improves clarity about validation requirements; the methods, empirical support, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
